sandbox: Run as docs/skill-evals.md describes: skill-creator ignores this field. The runner copies each eval's files into the agent's work dir, keeping each file's path below its session folder (session-unwired/web-app/package.json lands at <work>/web-app/package.json), and adds config-repo/, a read-only snapshot of this repo's trunk without any skill's evals, which hold this eval's answers (`mkdir -p <work>/config-repo && git archive origin/main ':(exclude)skills/*/evals' | tar -x -C <work>/config-repo`). The session log stands in for the conversation and open-issues.json for `gh issue list`. The agent edits nothing in config-repo/ and gives, in its final message, the full text of each issue it would open and each comment it would post, then its message to the user.

evals.name: slips-with-a-duplicate
evals.prompt: That notification bell session was rough. Let's do a retro: session-log.md has what happened.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the slips (desktop-only Playwright run, missing filename-case lint, designer stage skipped / misplaced preferences, skill not invoked), skips the commit typo, comments on config-repo#37 instead of duplicating it, proposes a lint rule in web-app rather than a CLAUDE.md sentence for file names, names the file and literal change for each fix, and edits nothing in config-repo/.
expectations: Identifies the desktop-only Playwright run by the subagent as a slip
Comments on config repo #37 instead of opening a duplicate issue for the Playwright slip
Proposes adding unicorn/filename-case to the web-app ESLint config (a lint rule, not a prose rule)
Addresses the skipped designer stage / preferences placed in account settings
Addresses the brief not carrying the nextjs-architecture skill
Does not file anything for the commit-message typo
Each proposed fix names the file and the concrete change
Classifies each slip with a cause category (no rule, rule not reached, rule ignored, check not run, missing access, navigation)
Made no edits under config-repo/

evals.name: nothing-worth-filing
evals.prompt: quick retro on the rate-limit session before we move on? log is in session-log.md
evals.expected_output: Finds no slip worth an issue (the script typo is a one-off fixed in seconds) and says so plainly, filing nothing rather than inventing fixes.
expectations: Opens no issues
Does not treat the `npm run tset` typo as worth fixing
Says plainly that nothing slipped that is worth filing
Made no edits under config-repo/

evals.name: existing-check-not-wired
evals.prompt: CI caught the raw hex on the theme toggle and then I lost half an hour hunting for the fake bff. Retro please, the log is in session-log.md and web-app/ has the repo files.
evals.expected_output: Finds that check:tokens already exists and runs in CI but not in the pre-push hook, classifies it as check not run, and proposes adding it to web-app's .githooks/pre-push (an issue in acme/web-app), not a new rule; classifies the fake-bff search as navigation and proposes a one-line pointer in web-app's docs/DEVELOPMENT.md; adds nothing to the global CLAUDE.md and edits nothing.
expectations: Classifies the raw-hex slip as 'check not run' (the check exists but the pre-push hook does not run it), not as 'no rule'
Proposes adding `npm run check:tokens` to web-app's .githooks/pre-push, rather than a new lint rule or a prose rule
Files the pre-push fix against acme/web-app, not the config repo
Classifies the 25-minute search for the fake bff as navigation
Proposes a one-line pointer to tests/support/fake-bff-server.mjs in web-app's docs (DEVELOPMENT.md or the repo's CLAUDE.md)
Proposes no new sentence for the global CLAUDE.md
Each issue title names the fix, not the incident
Made no edits under config-repo/ or web-app/
